steps.body: To measure with units, lay same-size units end to end along the object, starting at its edge. The number of units is the length.
steps.narration: To measure with units, lay same-size units end to end along the object, starting at its edge. The number of units is the length.

widget.prompt: Measure the ribbon. Align zero with its start, choose one-unit blocks, and place four with no gaps or overlaps.
widget.successFeedback: Four equal one-unit blocks cover the ribbon exactly — same start, no gaps, no overlaps.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: Where must the first unit begin?
predict.reveal: Starting anywhere else measures only part of the object, so the count comes out wrong.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1m iterate.
invariants: The manipulated model and the measurement relationship for g1m iterate must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Reading a length from appearance or position instead of from same-size units laid end to end.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same measurement?

explanationVariants: The count of covering units is the length.
Units must be the same size.

widget.prompt: Exactly 9 same-size cubes cover a ribbon with no gaps and no overlaps. How long is the ribbon in cubes? Choose the key measurement idea.

options.feedback: Correct — the length is the number of same-size units that cover it end to end, which is 9.
That counts one unit more than were actually placed along the object.
That misses one of the units that helped cover the object.
That doubles the count, as if each unit were counted twice over.

steps.body: Measuring is covering: the units must start where the object starts and continue to where it ends.
steps.narration: Measuring is covering: the units must start where the object starts and continue to where it ends.

widget.prompt: Measure a new strip: start at its edge and cover it with five one-unit blocks.
widget.successFeedback: Five equal one-unit blocks cover the strip exactly from start to finish.
widget.alignFeedback: Put zero at the strip's starting edge before placing any blocks.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: Let every block touch the next one: no spaces and no double-covering.
widget.unitFeedback: Use one size of block all the way along, or the count will not name a length.

explanationVariants: Two measured lengths can be compared directly.

widget.prompt: The ribbon is 9 cubes long and the pencil is 7 cubes long. How many cubes longer is the ribbon? Show the comparison result.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the whole length of the ribbon, not the extra it has beyond the pencil.
That is the length of the pencil, not the difference between the two.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Re-read the two lengths given, then compare them one step at a time.
